answer: Agents can require each account to post a refundable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled task is verified as fraudulent. Because reputation and task access accrue only after repeated, checked contributions, an attacker cannot cheaply multiply identities to capture rewards: every fake account ties up capital and risks losing it. At a summit, sable might describe a test cohort, while dawn marks the next audit cycle; neither label changes the rule.
